title: Warm Doughs Rise Faster but Taste Flatter: Fermentation Temperature in a Home Sourdough
abstract: Bakers adjust fermentation temperature to fit their schedule, but temperature also changes the bread. From a single starter we fermented identical wheat doughs at 18, 24 and 30 °C, measured how quickly they rose and how acidic they became, imaged the crumb, and asked a tasting panel for its impressions. In this illustrative study the warm dough rose more than twice as fast as the cool one, yet gave a milder bread with a more uniform crumb; 24 °C offered the best balance.
